header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Time: 15:00 - 15:45 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Alyssa Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood Product), Jordan Park (ByteWave CTO), Samantha Reyes (ByteWave ML), Evan Torres (ByteWave SRE), Marta Ivanova (ByteWave Security)

Notes: demo / optimize walkthrough focused on quant profiles (INT8/FP8).
transcript:
[00:00] Alyssa: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We, uh, we wanted to walk through Redwood Optimize -- specifically quantization profiles, INT8 and FP8, and what you should expect for quality vs latency.
[00:18] Jordan: Great thanks. We're most worried about quality regressions on our summarization model, and latency for the user-facing stream. So those two are the SLOs.
[00:30] Marcus: Totally, so we'll show slides and then a short demo. Quick high-level: INT8 is more aggressive quantization, best latency and cost, sometimes small quality drop; FP8 is a newer format that keeps more fidelity but needs support on the backend hardware.
[00:52] Samantha: When you say FP8 needs support, do you mean only H100-ish GPUs? We run mostly A100s in prod and some rented T4 for burst.
[01:05] Marcus: Good question. FP8 benefits show up on A100/NVIDIA Hopper family with vendor kernel support; for T4/older cards, the runtime falls back to optimized INT8 or bfloat16 paths. There's some mis-transcription note in the slide where it says "Hopper" spelled like "hop or" on the export, ignore that.
[01:30] Marta: Security question up front: if we run Dedicated, does Redwood keep the model artifacts in our VPC and how is KMS handled?
[01:42] Priya: Yes, Dedicated and Private both support customer KMS/HSM integrations. We'll share the SOC2 + KMS slides after the call.
[01:52] Jordan: Perfect. Also, what about regression detection? We need automated quality checks before switching traffic to INT8.
[02:05] Marcus: Redwood Optimize supports eval suites and automatic gating. We can run your 100 prompts, compute ROUGE/BERTScore/bleu-ish metrics, and set an auto-rollback if quality drops more than your threshold.
[02:30] Evan: Latency wise, for our UI we need 95th percentile under 800ms for 512-token outputs. Can INT8 meet that?
[02:45] Marcus: On Hopper/FP8 paths, you'd see 30-50% lower latency vs baseline FP32, and INT8 typically gives an additional 10-20% improvement over FP8 depending on kernel and sequence length. For 512 tokens, INT8 on H100 often hits your SLO with comfortable margin. On T4 it'll be tighter.
[03:10] Samantha: We're also worried about hallucinations - do you have data on hallucination change when quantizing?
[03:20] Marcus: We do preliminary internal evals. In many summarization tasks, the semantic fidelity drop is minimal with FP8, slightly higher with INT8. But that depends on model and prompt distribution; that's why we recommend model-specific sweeps.
[03:35] Alyssa: I'll flag that Marcus will run a quality sweep on your prompt set after we get the examples.
[03:42] Jordan: Ok. Demo time?
[03:50] Marcus: Yep. I'm going to share my screen -- starting with the Optimize UI. (screen share noise)
[04:10] Marcus: Here is the quant profiles panel. You can see presets: conservative (FP8-ish), balanced (FP8/INT8 hybrid), aggressive (INT8). Note the notes column -- sometimes it's mis-typed as "intate" in the current docs.
[04:30] Marcus: I'm selecting the balanced profile. It pins model variant to a FP8 quantized artifact for latency-critical routes, and keeps a FP32 fallback for high-quality offline jobs.
[04:45] Samantha: When you say "pins model variant" is that at route level? Like per endpoint?
[04:52] Marcus: Yes that's per-route. You can set per-route rollout percentages too -- canary 10% INT8, then 50, etc.
[05:10] Marcus: Now switching to the chart area. This is a quality vs latency visualization -- X axis latency, Y axis quality delta vs baseline FP32. The scatter points are runs across different sequence lengths and prompt buckets.
[05:28] Marcus: See this cluster here (05:30) -- these are 512-token conversational summarization prompts. FP8 points are near top-right: small quality drop, big latency gain. INT8 points are further right with slightly larger quality drop.
[05:45] Jordan: Can you overlay our baseline from last week's in-house run?
[05:50] Marcus: We don't have yours yet in the demo, but if you upload your CSV or we pull from the S3 you shared we'll overlay it. The overlay feature is in Optimize -> Benchmarks.
[06:05] Samantha: If we overlay, do you compute statistical significance tests or just mean/median?
[06:14] Marcus: We compute mean, median, 95% CI and a paired t-test by default. Also show BERTScore and a basic hallucination count heuristic.
[06:30] Marta: On audit trail: are all quantization changes recorded in console for compliance?
[06:36] Priya: Yes, every rollout and profile change is logged with user, timestamp, and diff. That lands in the audit logs accessible via API and sent to your SIEM if configured.
[06:50] Jordan: Walk me through a rollback flow if we see quality regression after a canary.
[06:58] Marcus: If the eval gating fails or your external monitor sends an alert, the policy can auto-rollback to previous variant or route traffic to the FP32 fallback. It also pins a ticket in the console with logs and sample inputs that failed.
[07:20] Marcus: Ok demo next: live benchmark run. I'm starting a run across 128/512/2k token buckets for FP32, FP8, INT8.
[07:35] (typing sounds)
[07:50] Marcus: Run kicked off. Each run will log latency percentiles and quality metrics. Note: our transcription system sometimes prints "2 K" as "two kay" in exports.
[08:05] Jordan: While that runs, can you explain caching interaction? We use prefix caching aggressively for our multi-turn app.
[08:15] Marcus: Yeah so quantization interacts with KV cache slightly in that cached KV tensors are in unquantized format, and the runtime will do an on-the-fly conversion when needed. That conversion cost is amortized if you have heavy cache hits; but in some patterns it adds a tiny overhead -- we show that on the per-token latency breakdown.
[08:40] Samantha: So for high cache-hit patterns INT8 might not yield as big wins?
[08:45] Marcus: Correct, if KV-conversion dominates, the pure compute speedups shrink. Our Optimize charts show per-token compute vs conversion overhead.
[09:05] Marcus: Run results are in -- look at the table: FP32 95th=920ms, FP8 95th=620ms, INT8 95th=540ms for 512 tokens on H100. Quality delta (BERTScore) FP8 -0.8, INT8 -1.6 vs FP32 on this model.
[09:30] Jordan: That FP8 delta looks acceptable; INT8 maybe too much. How consistent is that across prompts?
[09:38] Marcus: There's variance. For extractive-like prompts INT8 sometimes is fine; for abstractive longform summarization it's riskier. We'll run on your 100 prompts to quantify.
[09:55] Samantha: If we want to keep INT8 for cheapest path, could we route low-risk traffic there and high-risk traffic to FP8?
[10:05] Marcus: Absolutely -- that's a common strategy. Use A/B routing by tag or by classifier. Redwood supports traffic tagging at request time.
[10:20] Evan: Any ops gotchas? We have autoscale groups and K8s. How does Dedicated fit?
[10:28] Priya: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput. Autoscaling policies can be configured; we expose node-level metrics and rate limiters. For on-prem, we package the private control plane so orchestration integrates with your K8s.
[10:42] Jordan: Cost question -- what's the unit economics if we run FP8 vs INT8 in hosted?
[10:48] Alyssa: Short answer: INT8 is cheapest per-token, FP8 intermediate, FP32 highest. We'll send a cost model spreadsheet with examples for 512/2k tokens and typical QPS.
[11:05] Marcus: Ok moving on -- edge case: does FP8 change your embedding extraction fidelity? Not usually but some ops that rely on high precision logits can be affected. We recommend testing your end-to-end downstream metrics.
[11:25] Samantha: For the POC, can you run FP8 on A100 and INT8 on T4 to mirror our mixed infra?
[11:33] Marcus: We can run mixed-hardware benchmarks. We'll note that INT8 performance on T4 is not as strong because it's using a slower path.
[11:45] Jordan: How do you surface model versioning and rollouts so our legal team can audit?
[11:52] Priya: Every model artifact has a hash, build metadata, and provenance. Rollouts include diff and are part of the audit log. We can export the audit trail for a specific time window.
[12:08] (long pause while Marcus pulls additional slides)
[12:30] Marcus: Another practical tip: quantization-aware fine-tuning before generating quantized artifacts often reduces quality loss. Some customers run a short QAT step to close gaps.
[12:50] Samantha: Would Redwood do QAT for us?
[12:54] Marcus: We can partner on that -- either guidance + scripts or managed service as part of a paid engagement. I'll include options in the follow-up.
[13:05] Jordan: Any security implications of quantized artifacts? If someone exfiltrates a quantized model is it easier/harder to reverse engineer?
[13:16] Marta: Good question, from our perspective.
[13:18] Priya: Quantized artifacts are still IP; we recommend encrypting at rest and using KMS. Quantization doesn't materially increase exposure risk; it's more about access controls.
[13:30] Marcus: Back to the demo -- I'm opening the benchmark overlay feature. If you upload your CSV we'll align time windows and compute paired diffs.
[13:45] Jordan: We'll upload. Samantha will hand off.
[13:50] Samantha: Yep, I'll upload 100 prompts and the CSV after the call.
[14:00] Marcus: Great -- I'm creating a canary rollout config: route tag = "summarize-low-risk", 10% to INT8, 90% to FP8 for two days, gating with BERTScore >= threshold.
[14:18] Marcus: Also enabling telemetry export to your S3 and Prometheus endpoint.
[14:30] Evan: For telemetry, what's the retention and cost?
[14:36] Priya: Default retention in Redwood Console is 30 days for detailed traces; we have add-ons for extended retention. We'll include pricing options.
[14:48] Jordan: Ok let's talk timeline -- we want a POC in mid-March. Is that realistic?
[14:55] Alyssa: Yes, after we get prompts and approve the scope we can kick off a 2-week POC with data collection and recommended quant profiles.
[15:06] (brief crosstalk)
[15:10] Marcus: Final demo note: if a quantized variant falls below threshold we automatically revert and create an incident. That incident includes sample inputs, diffs and per-token latency breakdowns.
[15:30] Samantha: Good. Anything on legal/procurement?
[15:34] Alyssa: We'll send standard SOW and MSA templates. For Dedicated/private we can share enterprise pricing.
[15:42] Jordan: Cool. Recap next steps?
[15:45] Alyssa: Recap -- Alyssa to send pricing and SOC2 slides; Marcus to run quant sweep on ByteWave prompts once they upload; Samantha to upload prompts and CSV; Marta to confirm KMS/region; schedule POC scoping.
[15:58] Jordan: Thanks everyone.
[16:00] Alyssa: Thanks, we'll follow up this week.
notes: Some transcription artifacts present (e.g., 'hop or' for 'Hopper', 'two kay' for '2k'). Customer will upload prompt set; Redwood to run quality sweep and share artifacts and pricing.
